newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to unveil anti-tobacco strategy on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Canada to unveil anti-tobacco strategy on Thursday.

text.p: Canadian Health Minister David Dingwall said on Tuesday he would announce new anti-tobacco measures on Thursday.
He said in a statement he would announce "highlights of the federal government's new tobacco strategy to protect the health of Canadians, particularly young people."

Dingwall and his predecessor have been working on new measures since the Supreme Court struck down a ban on tobacco ads in September 1995 on the grounds of freedom of speech. He said two months ago a tax hike was one element being considered.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain.
Another major player is Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, owned 60 percent by Rothmans International, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
A third player is RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
